clue.text: Pressure to replace article in the end? That's as low as it gets (5)

definitions.text: That's as low as it gets

indicators.note: P takes the place of A, so the new letter sits where the article was

blocks.note: death is the end of life
P is the physics symbol for pressure
A is the indefinite article, and it is the letter swapped out of DEATH

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest point, asking whether it all ends in death under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: "In" places the swap inside DEATH; the definition is a whole phrase, since the depth of something is the lowest point it reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: The depth is the deepest point, as low as anything goes.

clue.text: Fool declines credit (8)

blocks.note: prices that decline dip
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A foolish person turning down an offer of credit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Declines" reads as refuses, but it is the verb dips; buying "on tick" is a British phrase for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dipstick is informal slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Pond-dwellers came and a pair reproduced (9)

indicators.note: reproduced means produced again, here in a new arrangement of the letters

blocks.note: CAME + A + PAIR, with "and" joining them

explanation.surface: Some pond creatures turned up in twos and bred.
explanation.walkthrough: Paramecia are single-celled organisms that do reproduce by dividing, so the surface is close to biology.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramecia are freshwater protozoa found in ponds.

clue.text: Excursion heading off after hot period (4)

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of TOUR comes off
after sets order in time or place, so the shortened excursion is placed behind the letter for hot

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
a tour is an excursion; without its first letter it is OUR

explanation.surface: A trip setting off after a spell of hot weather.
explanation.walkthrough: "Hot period" looks like a heatwave, but hot is only the letter H and period is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym at the loose end: sixty minutes is a fixed period, and the word also covers any spell, as in the hour of need.

clue.text: Distracted cast not currently performing (5,3)

blocks.note: to cast is to throw; past tense threw
an actor who is off is not on stage

explanation.surface: A theatre company in a daze on their night off.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cast" looks like the actors in a play, but it is the verb meaning threw.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone off is to distract them or put them off their stride.

clue.text: Time-study men, I now see, set up record year (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up turns the letters so they read upwards

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
oh is what you say when you suddenly understand
a log is a record, as a ship's log
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: Researchers timing workers, suddenly understanding, compile a record for the year.
explanation.walkthrough: "Time-study men" reads as efficiency experts, but the hyphenated phrase ends at study; men starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal Greek: hora means hour and -logy means study, so the word is built from exactly those two parts.

clue.text: Key American gym crew with time clocking mechanism (10)

blocks.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard
A is the abbreviation for American
PE is physical education, gym at school
a crew is a group of men
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A leading American gym team timing its workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: "Clocking" is a playful way of saying belonging to a clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The escapement is the part of a clock that releases its gear train one tick at a time.

clue.text: Eye doctor scrubbing cover of sealant round windows (5)

indicators.note: scrubbing removes letters
the cover of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: an oculist is an eye specialist
the outer letters of sealant, removed from OCULIST

explanation.surface: An optician cleaning off sealant around some windows.
explanation.walkthrough: "Eye" pulls toward the plural of oculus as eyes, but the definition is the architectural sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An oculus is a round window, as at the top of the Pantheon's dome; oculi is the plural.

clue.text: Article boring distant relative (6)

indicators.note: something boring into a word drills inside it

blocks.note: far means distant
THE is the definite article, set inside FAR after FA

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that bores a remote family member.
explanation.walkthrough: "Boring" reads as dull, but it means drilling through.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is a close relative, though the surface calls him distant.

clue.text: Piano lacking seventh note given away (5)

indicators.note: the word is lacking, so it loses, the letters named next

blocks.note: granted means given, handed over
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale, removed from GRANTED

explanation.surface: A piano missing a key, so given away.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts a piano with a note missing; the seventh note is the sol-fa syllable TE, not a key on the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortening: the full name of the large concert instrument drops its second word in everyday talk.

clue.text: Disorganised runners-up withdrawing names one after another (7)

indicators.note: disorganised letters are put in a new order
RUNNERS-UP withdraws, takes out, the two Ns

blocks.note: the letters of the fodder
N is the abbreviation for name; two names are two Ns, taken out

explanation.surface: A muddled bunch of second-placed finishers pulling their names from a race one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: "One after another" looks like it means in turn, but it is the definition: someone going after another person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic reading of an ordinary phrase: one who chases is literally one going after another person.

clue.text: Handled sports equipment - a scam, they say (7)

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a racket is a dishonest scheme, a swindle

explanation.surface: A bat or racquet sold as part of a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: "Handled" is literal: a racquet has a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A racquet is sports equipment with a handle, used in tennis or squash.

clue.text: Reportedly leaves something taken by the patient (4)

indicators.note: what is reported is spoken, so the sound counts

blocks.note: thyme is a herb whose leaves are used in cooking

explanation.surface: A patient said to be taking leaves, like a herbal remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: "Patient" suggests a hospital, but it is the adjective: a patient person takes their time.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a patient person is said to take their time, so it is the thing they take.

clue.text: England supporter hoping all playing finally contribute (10)

indicators.note: letters at play move around
take the final letter of contribute

blocks.note: the main letters of the fodder
the last letter of contribute

explanation.surface: An England fan hoping every player finally chips in.
explanation.walkthrough: "England supporter" reads as a football fan, but it means someone fond of England.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglophile admires England and English things.

clue.text: Relax fit for semi-formal attire (6,4)

blocks.note: to lounge is to relax
to suit is to fit, as in that suits you

explanation.surface: A dress code: relaxed but still fit for a smart occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fit for" reads as suitable for, but fit is the wordplay and for is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is a man's business suit, the standard for a semi-formal dress code.

clue.text: Bird sound from hen dropping large eggs (6)

indicators.note: dropping a letter lets it fall out

blocks.note: a hen clucks
L is the abbreviation for large, dropped from CLUCK
an O looks like an egg, so two eggs are OO

explanation.surface: A hen clucking as she lays big eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: "Bird sound" looks like the definition, but only "Bird" is; the cuckoo does famously lay its eggs in other birds' nests.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the cuckoo is a grey European bird named after its two-note call.

clue.text: School uniform summer shirt range (5)

blocks.note: a gam is a school of whales
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet
a T-shirt is the summer shirt

explanation.surface: A school's summer uniform comes in a range of shirts.
explanation.walkthrough: "School uniform" is a single idea in the surface, but school is a group of whales and uniform is a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from music: the gamut was originally the whole span of notes, hence the full extent of anything.

clue.text: Personal counsellor, priest that mostly messed up (9)

indicators.note: most of THAT, with its last letter gone
messed-up letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as it is
THAT without its last letter

explanation.surface: A personal adviser, a priest who largely made a mess of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A priest who counsels is plausible, which makes the wordplay hide in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A therapist counsels people individually.

clue.text: Not saying much about old Yorkshireman in the van (3)

indicators.note: the van is the front, as in vanguard, so take the first letter

blocks.note: C is circa, Latin for about
O is the abbreviation for old
the first letter of Yorkshireman

explanation.surface: A quiet old Yorkshireman riding in a van.
explanation.walkthrough: "Van" looks like a vehicle but is the vanguard, the front; Yorkshiremen are stereotyped as taciturn.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means reticent, unwilling to say much.

clue.text: Where to find the time and day some Biblical end arrives (8)

definitions.text: Where to find the time and day

indicators.note: only some of the letters are used, a run inside the phrase

blocks.note: biblicAL END ARrives, with the C from Biblical

explanation.surface: The day of reckoning, the end of days, finally arriving on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds apocalyptic, but the answer is inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the chart on the wall that sets out every day and date of the year.

clue.text: I go back and forth, write, and occasionally double up with a hint of mirth (8)

definitions.note: the clue speaks as the pendulum itself

indicators.note: taking letters on some occasions, every other one
a hint is only the first letter

blocks.note: to pen is to write
the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of double up
the first letter of mirth

explanation.surface: A writer pacing, scribbling, and now and then doubled up laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written in the first person, so "I" is the answer describing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A description in the answer's own voice: the weight in a clock swings to and fro.

clue.text: Trouble with inspiration for Springsteen? Quietly new drug embraced by support group (5)

indicators.note: the inner letters are hugged by the outer ones

blocks.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous
p is piano, quiet in music
N is the abbreviation for new
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Bruce Springsteen suffering writer's block, then entering rehab.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspiration here is breathing in; "for Springsteen" flags the American spelling, as British English writes apnoea.
explanation.definitionFit: Apnea is a pause in breathing, literally trouble with breathing in.

clue.text: Exist as an essential part where the definition ought to be (6)

definitions.text: where the definition ought to be

blocks.clueFragment: where the definition ought to be
blocks.note: the definition ought to be inside this very clue, so split the answer into two words

explanation.surface: A self-referential note about where a definition belongs.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half points at the clue itself: the definition ought to be in here.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a formal verb for being intrinsic to something, and, split into two words, a pointer to the clue itself.

clue.text: The first half of the alphabet at first is centrepiece of elemental building blocks (6)

indicators.note: take only the first letter of each of the next two words

blocks.clueFragment: The first half of the alphabet
blocks.note: A to M is the first half of the alphabet
the first letters of is and centrepiece

explanation.surface: An alphabet lesson treating the first thirteen letters as the core building blocks.
explanation.walkthrough: "Centrepiece" looks like a middle-letter instruction, but it only supplies its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic means relating to atoms, the building blocks of the elements.

clue.text: Exhausted genteel American behind mirror (5)

indicators.note: an exhausted word is emptied, leaving only its outer letters

blocks.note: genteel emptied of its middle
ass is American slang for the backside

explanation.surface: A tired, refined American admiring their rear in the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: "Exhausted" reads as tired, but it empties genteel; "behind" reads as position, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortening of looking glass, the old word for a mirror.

clue.text: Craft moral principles leader ditched for commercial treaties (5,5)

indicators.note: the leader, the first letter, is thrown away

blocks.note: a craft is a skilled trade
ideals are moral principles; without the I it is DEALS

explanation.surface: A politician abandoning principles to secure trade agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: "Leader" suggests a political leader, but it is only the first letter of ideals.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade deals are commercial agreements between countries.

clue.text: Panic contained by Territorial Army (5)

indicators.note: the answer is contained inside the next words

blocks.note: territoriAL ARMy

explanation.surface: Fear being kept under control by reserve soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a sudden fright.

clue.text: Palm and what's attached, a bunch of bananas (4)

blocks.note: the palm plus the fingers and thumb joined to it
the growers' word for one cluster cut from the stalk

explanation.surface: Holding a bunch of bananas in the palm.
explanation.walkthrough: The banana sense comes from the fruits' resemblance to fingers; each banana in the cluster is called a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the body part described piece by piece, and a trade term for a cluster of bananas.

clue.text: Briefly join detachment (4)

indicators.note: a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: to unite is to join; it loses its final E

explanation.surface: Signing up to a detachment for a short stint.
explanation.walkthrough: Join and detachment look like opposites, which hides that detachment is a military group.
explanation.definitionFit: A detachment is a military unit sent off on a separate task.

clue.text: Spoke like a Persian perhaps, but extremely misinformed about every vowel (7)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
M and D go about, around, the vowels

blocks.note: the first and last letters of misinformed
all five vowels, in the order the answer needs

explanation.surface: An Iranian speaking but getting every vowel wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: "Persian" looks like a person from Iran, but it is a Persian cat; the clue does not fix the order of the vowels.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaowed, or miaoued, is the sound a cat makes, so a Persian cat speaks by miaouing.

clue.text: Unreliable time indicator united island in revolt (7)

indicators.note: letters in revolt overturn their order

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for united
taken as it is

explanation.surface: A united island rising up against its rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sundial is unreliable because it only works when the sun shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundial tells the time, but not on cloudy days or at night.

clue.text: I'm kept nearby at regular intervals to follow church burial plot (8)

indicators.note: things placed at regular intervals are evenly spaced, so the letters are picked out with equal gaps, every second one
to follow is to come behind, so these letters are placed after the church abbreviation

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
the even letters of i'M kEpT nEaRbY

explanation.surface: A person kept close to a church, which suits a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's "I'm kept nearby" sounds like a speaker, but those words are just letters to thin out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a plot here is a piece of ground, and the answer is ground set aside for graves.

clue.text: Add space symbol (5)

blocks.note: to tot up is to add
an em is a printing space the width of an M

explanation.walkthrough: "Add space" sounds like a typing instruction; an em is a typesetter's unit of space.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an emblem, originally a natural object adopted as the sign of a clan.
